title: Concrete Genie
subtitle: Bring a town back with paint

body: Concrete Genie is Pixelopus's PlayStation 4 action-adventure, released on 8 October 2019. Ash uses a magical brush to paint living creatures across the walls of Denska, a neglected seaside town. His drawings supply companions and abilities that help him reach new areas and restore colour to the streets. The player builds scenes from collected designs, turning blank surfaces into small animated landscapes. The story connects that act of making something with Ash's experience of bullying, giving the town's recovery a personal purpose beyond opening another route.

Painted genies respond to Ash and can help solve obstacles around their walls. Different colours give them different powers, so choosing a creature becomes part of understanding what a location requires. Painting also asks the player to arrange the forms that make up each scene, making the wall visibly reflect those choices. The DualShock 4's motion controls support the movement of the brush. A puzzle and a drawing therefore share the same action: the player creates a companion whose ability can then change the way Ash moves through Denska.

The bullies move through the town and can threaten Ash or damage his paintings, asking the player to judge when it is safe to work. Restoring a ruined wall lets the activity continue instead of making its loss permanent. New designs and areas gradually enlarge the collection of things that can be painted. Dominic Robilliard directed the project, with Samual Marshall supplying the score. Reviewers generally welcomed its visual character and creative interactions. It became Pixelopus's final released game before Sony closed the studio in 2023.
